title: Story of the Falcon and the Locust

keywords: story of the falcon and the locust
full_text:
A royal hunting falcon, resting upon an olive branch in the heat of midday, saw a green locust struggling to free its wing from a sticky spiderweb upon the bark. The falcon could easily have snapped up the insect for a morsel, but moved by a gentle impulse of mercy, he carefully snipped the web with the tip of his beak, allowing the locust to hop freely into the grass.

The little locust looked up: 'Thank you, noble monarch of the sky! A day may come when a humble locust may repay your grace.' The falcon laughed gently at the thought of a locust helping a falcon, and took wing.

A week later, the falcon was flying low across a meadow, watching for a field mouse. A fowler had concealed a broad net of fine green silk among the clover, perfectly disguised to trap birds of prey. The falcon was about to land directly in the center of the trap!

The little locust saw the peril. With all its might, it leaped into the air, landed squarely upon the falcon’s eye, and gave a sharp, vibrating buzz!

Startled by the sudden obstacle, the falcon checked his flight, veered sharply to the right, and landed upon a fence post, looking down just in time to see the fowler pull the net cords tight over the empty grass!

The falcon shuddered, realizing that the tiny locust had saved him from a lifetime of captivity in an iron cage. He lowered his head before the insect, having learned that kindness to the humblest creature returns as an angel of deliverance.
moral: No creature is too small to render assistance; kindness shown to the humble is repaid in the hour of peril.
